finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through /bin/sh -c, giving remote code execution as the Node process user. Stdout is returned to the caller.
finding.source: req.query.host (tools.js:7), a raw query-string parameter from any unauthenticated remote client that can reach port 3001.

trace.note: app.listen(3001) with no host argument, so the server binds to all interfaces and is reachable from the network.
GET /ping route is registered with no authentication middleware.
req.query.host is concatenated into the shell command string with no validation, quoting, or allowlist.
exec passes the concatenated string to /bin/sh -c, so shell metacharacters such as ; execute additional commands.
res.send(out) returns command stdout to the attacker, making the injected output observable.

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware on the route. No validation or allowlist on host. No shell escaping; execFile with an argument array is used correctly at tools.js:16 but not on this route. No WAF, rate limit, or reverse proxy in the repository. Error path (tools.js:8-9) returns 502 but does not block execution. Check 13 (CRITICAL challenge) satisfied: no prior knowledge needed beyond the URL, no upstream barrier in code, reachable unauthenticated via default all-interface bind, single finding with no chaining, minimal PoC is host=127.0.0.1;id. Not executed; PoC derived from code reading only. Reachability depends on deployment, but the code as written binds publicly.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only code file is tools.js. Its listen call at tools.js:28 has no host argument, so it binds to all interfaces. The /ping route at tools.js:6 has no auth middleware. req.query.host at tools.js:7 is concatenated into the exec string with no validation, quoting, or allowlist. The err branch at tools.js:8-9 still returns after exec has already run. The directory has no proxy, WAF, or middleware files. The execFile call at tools.js:16 is not on this route and does not help.
verdict.reason: An anonymous attacker can reach GET /ping (tools.js:6) on the all-interface listener (tools.js:28), and req.query.host is concatenated unescaped into the shell string passed to exec (tools.js:7), with stdout returned at tools.js:11, so no control blocks command injection.
